label: text
text: That the man arrested by Chinese strike pickets at the Sam-chun border this week is not "an Englishman" is vouched for by a very reliable authority on the spot.

label: text
text: Last night a gentleman attached to the “Kowloon and district” station of the Chinese Maritime Customs (doing duty on the Chinese frontier adjoining the New Territories) came into Hongkong. He says that the person who crossed the boundary and was held by the pickets was a native of Shantung.

label: text
text: Conversation, heard indicates that the man claimed to be, or to have been a policeman in Hong Kong. As none of the Shantung police contingent has to be accounted for, it is presumed, if his statement is based on fact, that he was formerly in the force.

label: text
text: He was also heard to offer his services to the strikers as a “brother.” His 8vertures were at once turned down as his good intentions were suspected. He was seen to have been attacked forthwith and to have received a sound drubbing. Later on he was sent to Canton, in custody.

label: text

text: A second man was also caught and both came up at the Police Court this morning.

text: GOOD CHANCE TO SEE SUN'S ECLIPSE.

label: text
text: Sumatra this year attracted many scientists, several expeditions making it their point of observation of the total eclipse of the sun on January 14. But in May 1954, 28 years hence the Philippines and probably Manila will be their Mecca. From Manila they will observe and study an even more interesting and scientifically important eclipse, according to Father Selga, director of the Manila observatory.

label: text
text: The 1954 eclipse will be complete along a path which crosses the Philippines. The maximum totality of the sun's eclipse will last seven minutes, which is more than double (says the "Manila Bulletin") the maximum totality of the recent eclipse on the route that passed through Sumatra. In Sumatra the complete eclipse lasted only three minutes.

label: text
text: Whether the Philippines is picked as an observation point for international scientific expeditions may depend, however, upon weather conditions during the eclipse, Father Selga said. It is yet too far to determine the exact

text: DR. C. C. WU ADDRESSES MERCHANTS.

label: text
text: Dr. C. C. Wu, the present Mayor of Canton addressed a combined meeting of the four Chambers of Commerce of Canton on Wednesday on the subject of negotiations to end the strike and boycott.

label: text
text: Dr. Wu's speech followed the general lines of the text in English published in the "Canton Gazette" and since reproduced in Hongkong.

label: text
text: Incidentally the speaker admitted that both the Chinese labourers and merchants of Canton had suffered Heavy loss, with those of Hongkong.

label: text
text: Mr. So Shiu-ching, chairman of the Strike Executive also addressed the meeting, says the "Kung Sheung Yat Po."

label: text
text: There were about forty merchant representatives present, continues the report. After the meeting a resolution was passed unanimously. In view of its importance, a close translation is given which, if not quite grammatical, is best understood:—

label: text
text: "To-day Mr. Wu, the Mayor, has announced the unofficial negotiations between the (Canton) Government, and the Hongkong Government. This meeting declares itself to be satisfied that the present strike of labourers is actually of the people, and spontaneous. As the various friends in labour have made such great sacrifices and are so steadfast, we, the various merchants, should associate ourselves (with them) as one, steadfastly assisting, to attain to the object of Hongkong fully accepting the terms for resumption of work (ending the strike)."

text: The general tightness of money points to financial stringency in both business and social circles and it will occasion no surprise to see things quieter than usual.

label: text
text: Britain and America are ringing with the heroic rescue of the crew of the "Antinoe," which, in the terse seamen's language of the President Roosevelt's master, Captain Fried forms a thrilling epic of the sea.

label: text
text: Beginning on January 24, when the wireless compass bearings showed the "Antinoe's" own estimate of her position of a hundred miles to be an error, the "President Roosevelt" arrived and pumped out oil with excellent effect, but lost sight of the "Antinoe's" for 24 hours. She found her again on January 25, heavily listing to starboard. The engine fire room was flooded and the hatches broken.

label: text
text: Captain Fried ordered a lifeboat to be launched, whereupon a squall hit the ship and upset the boat, two men being drowned and the others rescued with difficulty in an exhausted condition and covered with oil.

label: text
text: Thereafter, until January 27, continued, fruitless, manœuvres were made to got in contact by means of lines fired by the Lyle gun, also by boat. The line broke sixteen times, until the apparatus was improvised at the suggestion of an artillery expert on board. Twelve men were got off on the afternoon of January 27 and the remainder at midnight, including the Captain, who was carried on board. They had been without food for two days.

label: text
text: The President Roosevelt's crew was in a state of collapse.

text: The Amerleo-Dutch expedition has been specially warned to take the utmost precautions owing to the Papua tribes' uncertain attitude toward foreigners.

label: text
text: The expedition is being organised under the auspices of the Dutch East Indies Committee of Scientific Research for the purpose of an eight months' exploration of the unknown territory in the region of the Nassau Mountains, New Guinea.

label: text
text: The purity will use an aeroplane specially constructed in accordance with instructions given by American round the world aviators. The base of operations will be Manokwari, which will be in wireless touch with Java.

label: text
text: The party, which will be armed, will include Professor Sterling, scientific leader; Dr. Van Leeuwen. Director of the Botanical Gardens, and Dr. BurtonZoorg, accompanied by a military detachment of 40 men and 180 native bearers. They leave for Manokvari at the end of March.
